cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: YOUR ONLY JOB IS TO DOCUMENT AND EXPLAIN THE CODEBASE AS IT EXISTS TODAY
cards.claim: The research phase is a pure documentation step with an explicit ban on suggestions, root-cause analysis, critique and refactor advice, so its output can be trusted as a map of current state.
cards.evidence_detail: Prompt rule only; no measurement of effect in the repo.
cards.landing: A research-only skill or agent for FixFlow diagnoses, kept separate from the planning skill; fits the knowledge-store design of verified diagnoses.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: research must stay objective about the current codebase, not be influenced by what a ticket wants to build
cards.claim: The research agent is forbidden from reading the ticket and works only from a questions file, so the task cannot bias the findings.
cards.evidence_detail: Prompt rule; the ticket file is explicitly off-limits to the research step.
cards.landing: Phase routine: a research step that receives only questions, not the phase goal; relevant to the P1 cold-resume trial design.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: GOOD QUESTIONS DO NOT LEAK ANY IMPLEMENTATION DETAILS OR THE NATURE OF THE TASK
cards.claim: A separate step turns the ticket into descriptive 'how does it work' questions (fewer than 8, with verbatim context pointers) that carry no hint of what will be built; the questions file is consumed only by the research step.
cards.evidence_detail: Prompt rule plus a template with four example question shapes and a Key Context Pointers section.
cards.landing: A question-writing skill ahead of any FixFlow research or diagnosis subagent; a way to blind refuters or cold-resume agents to the conclusion.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: DO NOT read research questions documents - research questions are inputs to the research phase only.
cards.claim: Each later phase (design, outline, plan) is told not to read the research-questions file and to use the completed research document instead, so intermediate artifacts are consumed once and not re-read.
cards.evidence_detail: Repeated in create-design-discussion, create-structure-outline and create-plan.
cards.landing: Context budget: a per-artifact read list for each phase so a fresh session loads only the artifacts it needs.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: plan > structure outline > design discussion > research > ticket
cards.claim: Artifacts carry an explicit precedence order, newest wins, and each skill restates the chain (later versions insert TDD and PRD), so conflicts between documents resolve mechanically.
cards.evidence_detail: Precedence strings appear in create-design-discussion, create-structure-outline, create-plan and the iterate skills.
cards.landing: Phase routine or CLAUDE.md: a one-line precedence rule between ship plan, phase PR plan, decisions journal and docs.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Chronological indexing: `ls` the task directory, find the highest existing NN- prefix
cards.claim: Every artifact in a task directory is named NN-type-slug.md with a zero-padded chronological index, so the folder reads as the history of the task and a fresh agent can see the order.
cards.evidence_detail: Naming rule used in all create-* skills.
cards.landing: Evidence folders and phase journals: a numbered artifact naming convention that helps a cold-resume agent find the latest document.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Read these files yourself in the main context before spawning any sub-tasks
cards.claim: The main agent must read every named input file in full (no limit/offset) before it spawns subagents, so decomposition is based on first-hand context.
cards.evidence_detail: Repeated as 'Use the Read tool WITHOUT limit/offset' across skills.
cards.landing: Workflow-tool orchestrator prompts: read the inputs fully before fan-out.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Do not use other agent types, including `general-purpose`, `Explore`, or `Plan`.
cards.claim: Research subagents are restricted to a small named set (codebase-locator, codebase-analyzer, codebase-pattern-finder, web-search-researcher), with 2-6 well-scoped agents rather than one per question, locators first then analyzers.
cards.evidence_detail: Prompt rule; also tells agents to return links and says foreground agents only in the outline skill.
cards.landing: Extend .claude/agents/fixflow-explorer.md into a locator/analyzer/pattern-finder trio; pin which agent types skills may spawn.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Don't write detailed prompts about HOW to search - the agents already know
cards.claim: Subagent prompts say what to find, not how to search, and the orchestrator is told to stay on synthesis and not deep file reading, to protect its own context.
cards.evidence_detail: Guidance bullets in create-research and iterate-research.
cards.landing: Workflow script prompt style; context budget of the orchestrator.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: This document will remain objective and factual. It does not contain any recommendations or implementation suggestions.
cards.claim: The research template carries its own 'methodology (verbatim)' paragraph and a git_commit/branch/date frontmatter, so a reader sees both the commit the facts were true at and the rule the writer followed.
cards.evidence_detail: Template frontmatter: date, git_commit, branch, repository, topic, type, tags, status.
cards.landing: Evidence folders / knowledge-store entries: stamp each diagnosis with the commit it was verified at.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: If there are no tests, say so explicitly — that's a finding
cards.claim: Every research section must record how that component is tested (locations, mocks, fixtures), and the plan and outline later reuse those patterns when writing test changes.
cards.evidence_detail: A 'Testing patterns' subsection per component in the research template; referenced by outline and plan skills.
cards.landing: Research or diagnosis template for FixFlow: a testing-pattern section feeding fail-before/pass-after tests.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: do at most one additional pass to find more information
cards.claim: After writing research, open questions get at most one more subagent pass; leftovers stay open and the human is offered three choices (find answers, answer themselves, discard).
cards.evidence_detail: Bounded loop plus a fixed three-option prompt.
cards.landing: Bound on refuter or diagnosis retries in workflow scripts; owner-facing 'open questions' prompt.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: It is **not a list of answers to the research questions**, and not a file index.
cards.claim: Documents must be written as a story with headers that state the takeaway (not the topic or the question), short paragraphs and each visual beside its prose, so a human can skim headers and learn how the system works.
cards.evidence_detail: Repeated in research, PRD, TDD and iterate skills with good and bad header examples.
cards.landing: Owner-view one-pager and phase PR bodies: takeaway headers; also a style rule for any CLAUDE.md-adjacent docs.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: You may recommend an option, but you must NOT resolve or close a question yourself
cards.claim: All design questions are written in the OPEN state; only the human can move one to 'Resolved Design Questions', and the resolved entry records the chosen option, rationale and the options discarded.
cards.evidence_detail: Template has Design Questions and Resolved Design Questions sections; final-answer template switches when hook context says all resolved.
cards.landing: Decisions journal in the draft PR: owner-only resolution of open questions, with rejected options recorded.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Exactly one question per message.
cards.claim: PRD and TDD are built as an interview: one question per message, and the document is patched only once a decision is resolved, not after each chat turn.
cards.evidence_detail: Same rule block in create-prd, create-tdd and their iterate- variants.
cards.landing: A grilling skill for owner decisions (ship plan gates); limits stacked questions to the owner.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: The doc is always a cohesive description of what's known - never a log.
cards.claim: After each resolved decision the agent re-works whole sections instead of appending, so the design document stays a current spec and not a changelog of answers.
cards.evidence_detail: Phrase 'Re-paint, don't append' in the iterate skills.
cards.landing: Rule for living docs such as the ship plan and CLAUDE.md: rewrite in place, journal separately.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Anything worth doing is worth measuring.
cards.claim: Every PRD must define a post-ship lever (metric, adoption signal, benchmark, error-rate target or qualitative read) as part of the definition of done, or record plainly that none fits.
cards.evidence_detail: PRD section 'What does business success look like, and how can we measure it?'.
cards.landing: Each FixFlow phase gets a stated check that proves it worked in production, not only in CI.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Do not open the Program Design phase until the user signs off on the System Design.
cards.claim: The design is split into System Design (across components) and Program Design (code shape), with a human review gate between them, and a PRD that stays in product space and defers technical items to a 'Deferred to TDD' list.
cards.evidence_detail: Ordered phases with explicit review-gate steps 4 and 6; PRD notes 'Deferred to TDD'.
cards.landing: Phase routine: owner sign-off on boundaries before in-slice code design; matches import-boundary contracts.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: The TDD should let the user decide, align, and re-steer the implementation
cards.claim: Design docs aim for leverage over exhaustiveness: the smallest set of diagrams, signatures and call-stack/file-tree/DI-map sketches that expose the decisions, with a code block in almost every program-design message.
cards.evidence_detail: Prompt rule; views listed: call-stack tree, component tree, file-tree diff, dependency-injection map, signatures, pseudocode.
cards.landing: Owner view and PR body: structural views (file tree, call tree) instead of prose changelogs.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Avoid horizontal phases like 'add all types', 'add API endpoints', 'implement UI'.
cards.claim: Phases must be thin vertical slices that cross layers and are each verifiable on their own; phase N must never need phase N+1 to be verified.
cards.evidence_detail: Prompt rule with horizontal vs vertical examples; echoes his 'vertical slices' fix in other work.
cards.landing: Ship-plan phase design check: each of the 40 phases is an end-to-end slice with its own verification.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: don't suggest manual testing for a step that could be automated w/ a script
cards.claim: Automated verification is preferred; manual steps are added only when needed, and a phase that cannot be manually checked is probably too small or not vertical enough; the goal is to avoid a 1000+ line change with no checkpoint.
cards.evidence_detail: Validation split into Automated Verification (runnable commands) and Manual Verification in outline and plan templates.
cards.landing: Phase acceptance criteria: runnable commands per phase; flag manual steps that could be scripted.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: The structure outline is our "c header files", the plan will include the function definitions.
cards.claim: Planning is split into a short structure outline (signatures, file trees, contracts, phase checkboxes) reviewed by the human first, and a longer plan with code diffs written only after the outline is accepted.
cards.evidence_detail: Two separate skills with outline-to-plan hand-off; outline carries a checkbox Implementation Overview.
cards.landing: Two-stage planning in the phase routine: cheap outline review before a full plan, to catch wrong direction early.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: DO NOT just accept the correction
cards.claim: When the human supplies a correction the agent must verify it (new research, read the named files) before acting, and treat all feedback as instructions to update the document, not to start implementing.
cards.evidence_detail: Repeated in iterate-design-discussion, iterate-plan, iterate-structure-outline, iterate-implementation.
cards.landing: Rule for agents handling owner comments: verify before acting; comments edit the plan, they do not start work.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: sha: [result of git rev-parse HEAD]
cards.claim: Every artifact's frontmatter records task, type, repo, branch and the HEAD sha it was written against; the plan template also has 'What We're NOT Doing', per-phase diffs, and success criteria split into automated and manual.
cards.evidence_detail: Frontmatter shared by outline, plan, PRD, TDD, design discussion templates.
cards.landing: Matches 'Plan @ <sha>' in the draft PR; extend to every journal or evidence file so staleness is checkable.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Not every phase requires manual validation, don't put steps for manual validation just to have them.
cards.claim: Plans include real code diffs and test code following patterns found in research, runnable automated checks, and a human pause between phases only where manual confirmation adds value.
cards.evidence_detail: Plan writing guidelines list.
cards.landing: Phase PR plan template: runnable verification per phase, no ceremonial manual checks.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: IMPORTANT - keep your prompt short, do not duplicate details that are already in the plan
cards.claim: Implementation is an orchestrator that launches one implementer subagent per phase with a short prompt ('implement Phase N, stop after automated verification'), then re-runs build/test/lint itself before reporting.
cards.evidence_detail: Orchestrator performs its own automated checks 'that the implementer agent may have missed'.
cards.landing: Saved workflow template: orchestrator plus phase implementer, with the orchestrator re-running checks (a cheap independent verifier).

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Pick up from the first phase without a ✅ marker
cards.claim: Progress lives in the artifact itself (checkboxes flipped on automated pass, a check mark on the phase title when all validation is confirmed), so a fresh session can resume from the document alone.
cards.evidence_detail: Resume rules in implement-outline and implement-plan (first unchecked item).
cards.landing: Cold-resume (P1): resume markers in the plan file, not in chat memory.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: don't commit or proceed to a next phase until the human has reviewed and approved the previous phase
cards.claim: By default the orchestrator commits and advances only after human approval, and multi-phase runs still use a separate implementer per phase with a pause only after the last.
cards.evidence_detail: Special Instructions sections.
cards.landing: Phase routine gate wording; one agent per phase maps to one phase per new chat.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: find the commit that marks the end of implementation
cards.claim: Follow-up work after implementation starts by diffing the current state, finding the end-of-implementation commit, and reading commits since, and unstarted phases still go to the implementer subagent rather than being done inline; for bugs the agent adds logging and asks the human to reproduce.
cards.evidence_detail: Steps 2 and 4 of the skill.
cards.landing: A fix-up routine for a phase PR after review: re-orient from commits since the phase ended.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Never commit dummy files, test scripts, or other files which you created
cards.claim: A non-interactive commit skill stages named files only (never -A or .), never commits the task artifact directory or stray scratch files, and never stops to ask for feedback.
cards.evidence_detail: Skill intended for CI/automated runs; 244 words.
cards.landing: A commit skill for FixFlow agents: explicit file staging and a ban on committing evidence or scratch folders.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Keep **Why the change** to exactly one sentence.
cards.claim: The PR body is capped at a one-sentence why, 1-3 reviewer warnings, and a compact structural change outline (SQL/endpoint contracts, file tree, component tree, call tree as diff blocks), with no walkthrough, verification checklist, changelog or plan-deviation section.
cards.evidence_detail: Template and step 4 of the skill.
cards.landing: Phase PR body format and the one-page owner view.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Never invent or guess a session URL.
cards.claim: The PR body ends with a machine-readable hidden comment 'HumanLayer-Session: <url>' taken from an environment variable or the newest stamped commit trailer, linking the PR to the session that wrote it; omit it if no source exists.
cards.evidence_detail: Daemon sets HUMANLAYER_SESSION_URL and a commit trailer; skill copies it into the body.
cards.landing: Provenance trailer on commits and PRs (session id or transcript path) so 'routine skipped' can be told from 'not consulted' after the fact; this is a hook-free form of a trace.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Stop and ask the user after 3 fix attempts on the same check.
cards.claim: After opening the PR the agent waits 5 minutes, checks mergeability, watches checks with --watch --fail-fast, fixes failures caused by the PR, reruns a flaky check once, and stops after 3 attempts; on merge conflicts it does not rebase but proposes a per-file merge plan and waits.
cards.evidence_detail: Step 8 with concrete gh commands and timeouts.
cards.landing: Closing step of the phase routine: bounded CI watch loop with attempt cap and a no-silent-rebase rule.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Only use when the user explicitly invokes this skill by name.
cards.claim: Nearly all RPI skills use this one description so the model never auto-selects them; the workflow is a fixed sequence the human triggers, and skill bodies are deterministic step lists, not discovery prompts.
cards.evidence_detail: Same description string on 20 of the 22 skills (configure-workspaces has its own).
cards.landing: Skills being added now: use a name-only trigger for phase skills so they never fire by accident and add no routing text to context.

cards.source_title: Skill layout: SKILL.md plus references/ templates and final_answer files
cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Respond following the selected template exactly. Do not include a summary or other information.
cards.claim: Each skill reads its artifact template and a fixed final-answer template from references/ only at the step that needs it (progressive disclosure), and the closing message is a fixed template chosen by environment checks (in a worktree or not, workspace disabled or not).
cards.evidence_detail: final_answer variants: plain, _in_worktree, _disabled, _resolved.
cards.landing: Skill authoring: move templates out of CLAUDE.md into on-demand references; the six-question closing message can be a template that forces comparable output.

cards.source_title: create-design-discussion / create-plan guidance on task directory
cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: the directory may be a symlink
cards.claim: The task artifact directory .humanlayer/tasks/ is a symlink into a separate repo and must not be committed, so skills forbid Glob/Grep on it and use ls -La; artifacts are shared and reviewed in a separate store, not in the code PR.
cards.evidence_detail: Warning repeated in nearly every skill; ci-commit and implement skills say never to commit it.
cards.landing: Where evidence folders and journals live (separate store vs in the repo); tool-compatibility trap for searching.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: <important if="the user asks you to find how things work or add detail about existing functionality">
cards.claim: Skill bodies use <important if=...> conditional blocks (with else-if branches) to say when a step applies, e.g. use subagents for 'how it works' questions and skip them when the answer is already in context.
cards.evidence_detail: Same conditional-tag pattern as his CLAUDE.md post, used inside skills.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md trim: wrap phase-specific sections in <important if> conditions so they apply only when relevant; skill bodies likewise.
cards.inventory_ref: (A3) Getting Claude to Actually Read Your CLAUDE.md

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: <important if="you are using the rpi:create-research skill">
cards.claim: The coordination repo's whole CLAUDE.md is three <important if=...> blocks, each keyed to a specific skill (repo list for any rpi skill; pull-latest check for create-research; worktree layout for setup-worktree), so each instruction loads only for its workflow.
cards.evidence_detail: CLAUDE.md of 43 lines in total.
cards.landing: The 390-line CLAUDE.md trim: key phase and skill rules to the skill being used, so they are inert otherwise.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: if not, propose pull commands to the user
cards.claim: Before research the agent checks every involved repo has the latest from its git remote and proposes the pull commands for the user instead of running them.
cards.evidence_detail: Example commands for origin/main and upstream/master.
cards.landing: Cold-resume and phase start: verify the checkout is current with remote before reading it as truth.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Run all your sessions from here
cards.claim: Human setup instructions live in HUMANS.md (README) and agent instructions live separately in CLAUDE.md, so humans' onboarding text never loads into agent context; sessions start from a sibling coordination repo that lists others via additionalDirectories and holds the shared skills and CLAUDE.md.
cards.evidence_detail: HUMANS.md and README are the same file except one note; CLAUDE.md has no setup prose.
cards.landing: Split FixFlow's human-facing text (owner notes, onboarding) from agent-loaded files; one place for shared agent config. Note CLAUDE.md here already has doc-map prose that is for humans.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: the Workspaces feature obviates the need for a standalone repo
cards.claim: The template itself says the product's Workspaces feature may replace the standalone coordination repo; only shared AGENTS.md and skills might still justify it.
cards.evidence_detail: Warning at the top of README; product doc link, no data.
cards.landing: nowhere obvious (multi-repo is not FixFlow's shape, single monorepo).

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Skills and instruction files (`CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`) are loaded from **all** repos in the workspace.
cards.claim: Per-task worktrees are set by a committed workspace.json (path and branch templates keyed to the task slug, source ref, setup command, additive copyGlobs for untracked env files) plus a gitignored local override; instruction files load from every repo but .claude/settings and MCP config only from the launch repo, so the repo with central policy should be primary.
cards.evidence_detail: Config schema and precedence rules; setup-worktree refuses to nest a worktree inside a worktree.
cards.landing: Worktree-per-phase config in this repo (already using worktrees); copyGlobs idea for env files; settings caveat applies to any multi-directory run.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Unless the user gives you a course of action, you MUST ask the user for clarification
cards.claim: Review comments on an artifact arrive as an XML block (quoted block with > marker, author, replies, [RESOLVED] tag) or via get/update/reply MCP tools; the agent offers a short menu (apply, apply and resolve, investigate and reply) and resolves or deletes only when told; deletion is a reversible tombstone.
cards.evidence_detail: Workflow plus comment_xml_format.md.
cards.landing: Owner review of plans and PRs via inline comments that the agent addresses one at a time, with an audit trail of resolved comments.

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: docker run --rm $(CLAUDE_MOUNTS) -e ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -it riptide-rpi-test -p "hi" --dangerously-skip-permissions
cards.claim: The only automated check of the plugin is a Docker smoke test that loads it and sends one prompt; the README adds a manual 'say set up rpi' prerequisite check; there are no per-skill behaviour tests.
cards.evidence_detail: Makefile targets build, test, shell; no eval files in the bundle.
cards.landing: Evidence that skill compliance is not measured even by the vendor; supports a cold-resume trial as the first real test.

gaps: Not read: describe-pr HTML files (pr_walkthrough_example.html, ref_code_slides template and guide) and scripts/inject-walkthrough-diffs.sh, create-tdd/iterate-tdd artifact_template.html, show-me.md reference files (each is one word, likely a pointer).
iterate-prd and iterate-tdd were read only for their first ~40 lines; remaining sections (Continue Grilling Mode etc.) not read, assumed to mirror create-prd and create-tdd.

The subagents the skills call (implementer-agent, outline-implementer-agent, codebase-locator/analyzer/pattern-finder, web-search-researcher) and the hooks that produce cloud permalinks and the session trailer are not in the bundle, so their prompts and any enforcement behaviour are unseen.
riptide-rpi repo bundle contained only a README; no skills folder was found there (skills are in the plugin directory inside humanlayer/humanlayer).

Authorship of the skills is not stated in these files; all cards use Dex+others. Dates are estimated: plugin.json shows version 0.50.0 with no date; riptide-rpi and template dates come from the inventory.
No measured numbers appear anywhere in this bundle; every card is asserted or marketing.
